claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy contains no additional self-lubricating phases.
A small amount of a carbide- or oxide-forming precursor will be introduced into CoCrFeNi.
The precursor will generate lubricious oxide or carbide phases in situ during sliding.
The generated lubricious phases will form a continuous network along the wear interface.
The precursor will react with oxygen or other available elements under sliding conditions.
The reaction products will form a stable, lubricious protective tribolayer.
The protective tribolayer will reduce metal-to-metal contact.
Reduced metal-to-metal contact will lower friction.
Reduced metal-to-metal contact will lower wear.
The modified alloy will have a significantly lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi from room temperature through 800 °C.
The modified alloy will have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi from room temperature through 800 °C.
The performance improvement will be especially pronounced near 800 °C.
The expected improvement depends on an environment that supports in-situ formation of the lubricious phase, such as one with sufficient oxygen.
The expected improvement is limited to mechanical loads similar to those used in standard sliding-wear tests.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi has difficulty maintaining low friction and wear rates across the full temperature range.
Failure to observe either a statistically significant friction or wear reduction, or the proposed tribolayer, is specified as falsifying the hypothesis.
